title: Center-fit gains exceed sampled-noise tests for 40 fixed profiles in 62 K2-22 Campaign 1 orbits
abstract: We test whether fixed asymmetric profiles explain apparent transit-center changes in 62 selected K2-22 Campaign 1 orbits. A shared-shape search tests 36 two-sided exponentials, three Gaussians and a box, with exposure integration. Separate centers give gains beyond all 399 noise trials for each of 40 fixed generating profiles in both K2SFF v1 and EVEREST v2.0. Gains are 2.35 and 4.85 times the largest simulated 99th percentiles. Every trial repeats the full search. Quadratic baselines retain the excess in a fitted-generator check. The result extends a prior symmetric-template study but does not establish orbital timing changes or a new planet. The noise law is estimated outside transit, fitted amplitudes are held fixed, the profile family is limited, and both reductions share photons. Variable dust shape, unmodeled noise and reduction errors remain possible. Code, aggregate tests, figures, input hashes and external retrieval steps are included. Raw observations and event tables remain outside the baseline package.
